hook_text: It wasn't underground. It wasn't a railroad. And it carried thousands of people to freedom.
clip_script: The Underground Railroad was a secret network of people who helped enslaved Americans escape to the North and Canada. Guides were called conductors. Hiding places were stations. The escapers were passengers. And the most famous conductor was a small, tough woman named Harriet Tubman. Born enslaved in Maryland, she escaped in 1849, walking by night, following the North Star. She could have stayed free. Instead, she went back. About thirteen times. She led about seventy people out, including her own parents. She started on Saturday nights, because runaway adverts couldn't be printed till Monday. She used disguises and songs as signals. Slave owners offered rewards for her capture. They never caught her. As she put it: I never lost a passenger.
visual_style: A whiteboard night forest with the North Star; a line of figures following a small leader; a house with a lantern in the window marked station; a reward poster blowing away.
pacing: Riddle hook, quick code words, a heroic climax.
